response.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.ordertune, f.rebtotal, f.rebrate, f.feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault), b AS (SELECT AVG(rebtotal) AS base FROM m) SELECT m.orderslink, m.ordertune, AVG(m.rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG((m.rebrate - m.feerate) / m.feerate) AS avg_relative_gap, AVG(m.rebtotal) - (SELECT base FROM b) AS excess_over_baseline FROM m GROUP BY m.orderslink, m.ordertune HAVING AVG(m.rebtotal) > (SELECT base FROM b) ORDER BY excess_over_baseline DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The baseline is the plain average of rebtotal over all matched fee records (inner join to orders), not an average of the group averages, as the request states.
orders.recordvault is unique, so the join does not duplicate fee rows.
Fee records with feerate = 0 give a NULL relative gap in SQLite (division by zero). AVG skips these NULLs, so they are left out of the average gap but still count toward the average rebate.
Fee records with a NULL rebtotal are ignored by AVG in both the group averages and the baseline.
